Consult Summary:
- Acute asthma exacerbation with chest tightness, wheeze, and shortness of breath on a background of recent viral URI; plan includes renewed inhaled therapy, a short course of oral steroids, and spacer use; advised rest and self-certification for 7 days with precautions and follow-up if symptoms worsen.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Chest tightness for ~3 hours; mild dyspnea; wheeze; nonproductive cough; sore throat and runny nose after a recent cold; symptoms persistent, with worse at night.
- Associated symptoms: Runny nose, sore throat; still feeling under the weather.
- Negative findings: No chest pain reported.
- Past medical history: Asthma (longstanding); hay fever; dust allergy; eczema in childhood; milk protein allergy in childhood; prior severe asthma exacerbation requiring intubation in adolescence.
- Medications: Inhalers previously used — Ventolin (Salbutamol) and Clenil Modulite (beclomethasone) — currently not in possession (ran out about 1 week ago); no current systemic steroids documented.
- Allergies: None documented.
- Family history: Mother with eczema; father with asthma.
- Social history: Not detailed; advised to rest; can self-certify 7 days off work.
- Review of systems: Cough with wheeze; shortness of breath on exertion; no reported sputum production.

Examination:
- Not documented.
- Vital signs: Not provided.
- Physical examination findings: Not provided.

Impression:
- Likely asthma exacerbation on a background of recent viral URI with wheeze, nonproductive cough, and exertional dyspnea; history includes past significant asthma with prior hospitalization.

Plan:
- Inhaled therapies: Prescriptions for Ventolin (Salbutamol) and Clenil Modulite; use specified as morning dose with Ventolin PRN; plan to deliver within the hour.
- Short course of oral steroids: Five days; two tablets in the morning; discussed potential side effects and labeling.
- Spacer: Provide spacer with instructions to use (prime, inhale/exhale, 5–10 breaths); education included; patient already aware but another spacer provided.
- Monitoring and safety: If Ventolin required more frequently than every 3 hours, seek medical attention.
- Activity and work: Rest; self-certification for 7 days off work.
- Follow-up: Return if symptoms worsen or if there is any concerning development; no formal follow-up appointment noted beyond acute management.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vitals and objective exam findings were not documented; no peak flow measurement available.
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Some audio cut-in/out segments noted; overall understandable; no critical data missing beyond the absent vitals/exam.
